key_insight: A multimodal model that combines ultrasound images, clinical data, and text descriptions improves fine-grained differentiation between breast fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumor, which often look similar on ultrasound.
clinical_relevance: Better preoperative classification may help clinicians reduce misclassification of borderline phyllodes tumors as fibroadenomas and improve decision-making.
method: Built FAPT-M, a pathology-confirmed multimodal dataset of 910 patients with ultrasound images, structured clinical attributes, and diagnostic text.
Used DenseNet for image encoding, CLIP-inspired text encoding, and lightweight clinical encoding.
Added clinical-conditioned modulation, cross-modal Transformer fusion, and dual-path representation learning to align and integrate modalities.
evidence_signal: On patient-level five-fold cross-validation, the method reached 77.64% accuracy, 73.38% F1-score, and 89.74% AUC, outperforming several CNN, Transformer, and vision-language baselines.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a single curated dataset, so external validation across centers and imaging protocols is still needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Multimodal Fusion for Fine-Grained Classification of Breast Fibroadenoma and Phyllodes Tumors
